Lolcat
LOL-kat
noun (Millennial slang)
A photograph of a cat with a caption in deliberately broken English ("lolspeak"), from LOL + cat. It grew out of 4chan’s "Caturday" image threads around 2005–2006; the site I Can Has Cheezburger?, launched in January 2007 and named for its most famous caption, made lolcats a mass phenomenon and an internet business. Lolspeak spread widely ("I can has," "ceiling cat is watching you," "invisible bike"). A crowd-sourced LOLCat Bible Translation Project (begun 2007) rendered Scripture in lolspeak.

Biblical Definition

A lolcat is a cat photo with a misspelled, baby-talk caption: "I can has cheezburger?" The genre was the Millennial internet’s first great comic form, and it turned house cats into an industry. The Christian observation: much of this is innocent and even good. Delight in animals is a biblical thing. God made the creatures and saw that they were good; He gave man dominion over them with responsibility, and "A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast" (Pro 12:10). The Lord feeds the birds and knows the sparrow’s fall (Mat 10:29). Laughing at a cat’s absurdities is a small enjoyment of creation. Two cautions are worth noting. The first is time: lolcats were the beginning of the endless scroll of cute and funny animals, and an evening of it is an evening gone. "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil" (Eph 5:16). The second is irreverence: lolspeak culture produced a running joke in which God was "Ceiling Cat," and a full lolspeak paraphrase of the Bible. Christians can laugh at cats and still refuse to make the Lord a punchline. "Holy and reverend is his name" (Psa 111:9). A father lets his children enjoy the funny cat pictures, teaches them to care for real animals kindly, and makes sure they know that the Creator of the cat is not a joke.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial internet genre (4chan c. 2005; I Can Has Cheezburger?, 2007) of captioned cat photos in "lolspeak"; innocent delight in creation (Pro 12:10), with cautions about wasted time and lolspeak’s irreverent "Ceiling Cat" jokes about God (Psa 111:9).

Pro 12:10 — "A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel."

Gen 1:25 — "And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good."

Mat 10:29 — "Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father."

Eph 5:16 — "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil."

Psa 111:9 — "He sent redemption unto his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend is his name."

Modern Corruption

Lolcats are innocent delight in God’s creatures; their shadows are hours lost to the scroll and a lolspeak culture that made God a joke.

expand to see more

The small corruptions are time and reverence. The captioned cat began a stream of cute content that never ends, and an endless stream is a thief of hours. The lolspeak culture around it also made a habit of turning God into a joke character, and a generation that laughed at "Ceiling Cat" was learning, a little, to treat the Lord as material. That is not a small thing to the One who said He would not hold guiltless those who take His name in vain.

The redemption is wonder at the creatures. "And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good" (Gen 1:25). Cats are funny because God made them so. Teach children to laugh at the cat, to feed and care for it well, to put down the phone when the scroll has gone on too long, and to give thanks to the Maker of every whisker.
